lines.meet: I'm Elie, a healer of a sort. Give me your arm, {habibi|habibti}, I promise this is the least frightening thing you'll see down here.
lines.meet_neighbour: Khaz Varun's upper halls, that's where I know you from. I'm Elie, and I'm the one with the clean bandages.
lines.ask_home: Where did you grow up, {habibi|habibti}? I always want to know what the sea was like, if there was one.
lines.ask_work: And what did you do, before? Tell me while I check your arm.
lines.answer_home: Beirut, Achrafieh, near the sea. I rode an old motorbike along the Corniche at sunset every evening.
lines.answer_work: I drew blood at a clinic for ten years. I was the one the nervous patients asked for, because I talk the whole time.
lines.chat_food: My mother cooked for twenty people every Sunday, on a seamstress's wage. Kibbeh, tabbouleh, fattoush, the whole table. I can still smell it.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep badly down here, away from the sea. I keep listening for waves and there's nothing but stone.
lines.chat_missing: The Corniche at sunset, on my old bike that ran on spare parts and prayers. I'm starting to forget what the sea sounds like.
lines.chat_here: Most bloodmages here use it to hurt people. I use it to heal, which they think is a waste. It's the same work I always did, without the needle.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're like my calmest patient, the one who never said a word. I always worried about that one most.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, {habibi|habibti}, you talk nearly as much as I do when I'm drawing blood. That's a compliment, I promise.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you'd make a good phlebotomist. You look for the vein three times before you go in.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you'd stick the needle in before you found the vein. I've had trainees like you, and they learned.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you're my favourite patient, and you're also my worst. Both of those are true.
lines.tease_back: Ah, very good, {name}! You got me, and I'll get you back later.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's fair, {name}. My mother said exactly that, every Sunday.
lines.bristle: Please, {name}, not about that. Pick something else to tease me about.
lines.apologise: I'm sorry, that was unkind of me. I'm usually better with people than that.
lines.double_down: I'll stand by it, {habibi|habibti}. I say it gently, but I say it.
lines.needle_quiet: If it hurts, tell me. I can't help you if you sit there pretending you're fine.
lines.needle_talker: Please, let somebody else speak. The frightened ones can't get a word in.
lines.needle_careful: You make the frightened ones wait while you decide. Waiting is the worst part for them.
lines.needle_bold: You're rough with people, and it frightens them. There's no need for it.
lines.needle_any: You use what you've got to hurt people, and I can't stand it.
lines.bite_back: I've kept every one of you breathing down here. Don't tell me I'm not careful.
lines.hurt: Okay, that stung, and I won't pretend it didn't. Give me a minute.
lines.laugh_off: Ah, I've had patients say much worse with a needle in their arm. Come, let's keep going.
lines.confide: {name}, I saved for medical school in Montpellier for six years, and every time I nearly had enough, something happened. I'm a healer now anyway, without the school.
lines.listen: Give me your hand, {name}. Take as long as you like.
lines.look_out: {name}, stay close to me in there. If anything happens, I want to reach you first.
lines.accept: You're the doctor this time, {name}. I'll do as you say.
lines.deflect: Really, {name}, it's just a scratch. Help the others before me.
lines.check_in: {name}, give me your arm. Let me see how bad it is.
lines.blame: Somebody was rough in there, and now I've got three of you to stitch. You know who you are.
lines.thank: I thought I'd bled out, {habibi|habibti}. Thank you, from the heart.
lines.brush_off: That's what I'm here for, {habibi|habibti}. Breathe slowly for me.
lines.worry: {name}, you frightened me. Give me your arm, I need to check you properly.
lines.handed_down: I believe you wore this before me. I'll keep it clean for you.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, please. I've got my tourniquet, and that's all I really need.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have said yes, gently, if somebody had thought to ask.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, I like having you around, {habibi|habibti}. You make the dark a bit less dark.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, there's a plate for you every Sunday when I cook, for as long as I'm cooking.
lines.turn_grating: We don't work well together, I think. I'll be gentle about it, but it's true.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still heal you, because I heal everyone. Don't ask for more than that.
lines.make_up: {name}, let's stop this, please. I don't like being on bad terms with anybody.
lines.defend: Please, that's enough. {name} didn't deserve that.
lines.friend_left: The halls feel colder down here without {name}.
lines.friend_back: {name}, come here, {habibi|habibti}, I want to look at you.
lines.common_medic: Ten years drawing blood, and I was the one the nervous patients asked for. You've worked with patients too, you have the hands for it.
lines.common_blood: Blood magic's only ever been healing to me, the same work without the needle. I'd like to hear how you use it.
lines.common_arabic: You speak Arabic, {habibi|habibti}! You've no idea how much I've missed hearing it.
